thread:
alex: FYI — customer WG (healthtech pilot) pushed for two things: shorter commit duration (3mo) and stricter data-retention add-on (30d on Dedicated). They also want pricing tier with per-tenant token caps + an SLA for p95 latency on Dedicated. Need a product decision by EOD Fri so legal/sales can draft terms.

maria: can we get a quick summary of the ask vs our current offers? I don't want to rehash the whole thread in legal.

jen: sales here — summary: customer wants 3mo reserved (instead of 12mo), ability to opt into 30d retention (default 90d), and a microtier that has a hard token ceiling per month (50M tokens) with optional burst top-up credits. They need enterprise SLA on p95 <= 150ms for text-gen on dedicated for <1k concurrent requests.
\

dylan-biz: 3mo commit is risky for revenue predictability. we could offer a pilot contract: 3mo minimum at a higher $/token, with an option to convert to 12mo at a discount. That preserves revenue while giving them flexibility.

sam: two parts to decide: packaging (tier vs addon) and contract shape. Packaging options (quick):
```
Option A: Microtier (50M tokens/mo) + optional burst pack (prepaid credits)
Option B: Standard tier w/ enforced hard cap (overage blocked) + add-on retention 30d
Option C: Pilot seat = temporary 3mo reserved bucket at premium rate, converts to commit
```
We should map each to launch criteria (SLA gating, infra readiness, billing flow changes).

alex: exactly. For launch gating I propose minimal criteria:
- infra: billing enforces hard caps and top-ups
- infra: retention toggle applied to tenant-config and purge jobs tested
- runtime: p95 < 150ms on dedicated during load test
- legal: template contract with 3mo pilot clause

jen: customer will only sign if SLA and 30d retention are available. they asked for standard contract language for SOC2/data retention. they also want limited audit logs retained 1yr; that's on the compliance side.

maria: technical tradeoffs: 30d retention removes caching benefits (prefix caching, kv cache TTLs). That will raise cost; need estimate.

dylan-biz: ask finance for delta. rough calc: removing 60d of KV cache saves them privacy but increases our token cost by ~8-12% on their workload (ballpark). We can offer a higher $/token tie for 3mo pilot to cover that.

sam: also need to decide whether hard cap is enforced at routing layer (reject) or at billing threshold (bill overage). Engineering work differs a lot.

alex: engineering preference? @eng-platform please chime in — we need an ETA for implementing enforced hard caps + retention toggle.

deploy-bot: scheduled load test for dedicated-staging at 2026-04-02T22:00Z. Results will include p50/p95/p99 latencies and error rates.

jen: ok — next steps I propose:
- Sales (jen) to confirm customer is OK with pilot pricing premium by EOD Thu
- BizOps (dylan-biz) to produce revenue/impact delta by EOD Thu
- Eng (sam/maria) estimate effort: hard cap + retention toggle + billing hooks by Mon
- Legal to draft 3mo pilot contract template with SOC2/retention clauses

sam: initial eng estimate — hard cap enforced at routing: 2w (changes to quota service + request-path checks). retention toggle + purge jobs: 1w. Billing/top-up MVP: 1w. Total parallelizable work ~2w with 2 engineers.

maria: QA note — need smoke tests to verify no cross-tenant cache leakage when retention lowered. Also add telemetry for cache miss rate, token spend delta per tenant.

alex: thanks. I'm going to run this at the product sync in 30m. If we can lock on Option A vs B vs C before then, we'll take it to GTM.

jen: I'll ping the customer about pilot premium and ask for flexibility on audit logs.

dylan-biz: I'll model scenarios and flag which ones hit revenue targets.

sam: tagging followups:
- action: eng estimate doc link: https://redwood.internal/eng/estimates/2467 (placeholder)
- action: runbook for cap enforcement

alex: :eyes: all good — will report back post-sync.
